nodes.name: Caliph Abdullah al-Mahdi Billah (Founder of Fatimid Caliphate, 909–934 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Ibn al-Athir, Al-Maqrizi, Lane-Poole.

nodes.name: Caliph Al-Mu'izz li-Din Allah (Founded Cairo & Al-Azhar, 969 CE)
nodes.notes: Conquered Egypt in 969 CE and founded Al-Qahirah (Cairo) & Al-Azhar Mosque.

nodes.name: Caliphs Al-Aziz Billah & Al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah (975–1021 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Ibn al-Athir, Al-Maqrizi, Lane-Poole.

nodes.name: Caliph Al-Mustansir Billah (60-Year Reign; Father of Nizar & Al-Musta'li, 1036–1094)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Ibn al-Athir, Al-Maqrizi, Lane-Poole.

nodes.name: Imam Nizar ibn al-Mustansir (Progenitor of Nizari Ismaili Imamat / Aga Khans, 1045–1095)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Caliph al-Mustansir; Alamut Nizari Imamat line continuing to Living Aga Khan V (2026).

nodes.name: Caliph Al-Musta'li → Al-Adid (Final Fatimid Caliph, d. 1171 CE)
nodes.notes: Younger son Fatimid succession to Al-Adid (d. 1171 CE).

nodes.name: Najm ad-Din Ayyub & Asad ad-Din Shirkuh (Patriarchs of the Ayyubid Dynasty, d. 1173 CE)
nodes.notes: Kurdish generals from Dvin (Armenia) who united Syria & Egypt; father & uncle of Saladin.

nodes.name: Sultan Al-Adil I (Saphadin; Brother of Saladin, Negotiated with Richard I, 1200–1218)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Al-Maqrizi, Modern Universal History Vol. 2–3.

nodes.name: Sultan Al-Kamil of Egypt (1229 Treaty of Jaffa with Emperor Frederick II, 1218–1238)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Al-Maqrizi, Modern Universal History Vol. 2–3.

nodes.name: Sultana Shajar al-Durr of Egypt (1250 CE; Transition to Mamluk Sultanate)
nodes.notes: Widow of al-Salih Ayyub who defeated Louis IX's crusade and wed Mamluk Sultan Aybak.

nodes.name: Mamluk Sultan Al-Mansur Qalawun (Qalawunid Dynasty Founder, 1279–1290 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Al-Maqrizi, Modern Universal History Vol. 2–3.

nodes.name: Sultan Al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun (Architectural Peak of Mamluk Cairo, d. 1341)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Al-Maqrizi, Modern Universal History Vol. 2–3.

nodes.name: Mamluk Sultan Al-Ashraf Qansuh al-Ghuri (Fell at Marj Dabiq 1516 vs Selim I)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Al-Maqrizi, Modern Universal History Vol. 2–3.

nodes.name: Emir Yusuf ibn Tashfin (Almoravid Founder of Marrakesh; Battle of Sagrajas 1086)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Mariana General History of Spain 1699, Ibn Khaldun.

nodes.name: Ibn Tumart & Caliph Abd al-Mu'min (Almohad Caliphate Founders, 1121–1163 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Mariana General History of Spain 1699, Ibn Khaldun.

nodes.name: Caliph Abu Yusuf Yaqub al-Mansur (Patron of Ibn Rushd; Koutoubia & Giralda, 1184–1199)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Mariana General History of Spain 1699, Ibn Khaldun.

nodes.name: Sultan Muhammad I ibn al-Ahmar (Founder of Nasrid Emirate of Granada & Alhambra, 1238)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Mariana General History of Spain 1699, Ibn Khaldun.

nodes.name: Sultans Yusuf I & Muhammad V of Granada (Alhambra Palaces, 1333–1391 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Mariana General History of Spain 1699, Ibn Khaldun.

nodes.name: Sultan Muhammad XII / Boabdil of Granada (1482–1492 CE)
nodes.notes: Surrendered Granada to Ferdinand & Isabella in January 1492 CE.

nodes.name: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi (Father of Algebra & Algorithms, House of Wisdom, c. 780–850)
nodes.notes: Coined Algebra (Al-Jabr) & Algorithm at Caliph Al-Ma'mun's House of Wisdom in Baghdad.

nodes.name: Al-Kindi (Baghdad) & Al-Farabi ('The Second Teacher' After Aristotle, c. 801–950 CE)
nodes.notes: Translated and synthesized Greek philosophy across the Abbasid world.

nodes.name: Abu Rayhan al-Biruni (Geodesist, Astronomer & Author of Chronology of Ancient Nations, 973–1048)
nodes.notes: Measured Earth's radius and compiled synchronous world royal genealogies at Ghazni.

nodes.name: Omar Khayyam (Astronomer, Mathematician & Poet of Nishapur, 1048–1131 CE)
nodes.notes: Reformed the Persian Jalali solar calendar under Sultan Malik-Shah I.

nodes.name: Nizam al-Mulk (Seljuk Grand Vizier & Founder of Nizamiyya Universities, 1018–1092 CE)
nodes.notes: Statesman serving Alp Arslan & Malik-Shah I; patron of Al-Ghazali & Omar Khayyam.

nodes.name: Ibn Rushd / Averroes (Philosopher & Qadi of Cordoba & Marrakesh, 1126–1198 CE)
nodes.notes: Chief judge of Seville & Cordoba; famed commentator on Aristotle under Almohad Caliphs.

nodes.name: Muhammad al-Idrisi (Andalusi Geographer; Tabula Rogeriana for Roger II, 1100–1165 CE)
nodes.notes: Created the world atlas Tabula Rogeriana at King Roger II's court in Sicily.

nodes.name: Ibn Battuta of Tangier (75,000-Mile World Traveler to Granada, Mali, Constantinople & China, 1304–1369)
nodes.notes: Recorded firsthand eyewitness accounts of Granada, Mansa Sulayman of Mali, Kilwa, Byzantium, Delhi & Yuan China.

nodes.name: Ibn Khaldun of Tunis (Founder of Historiography & Sociology; Met Tamerlane 1401, 1332–1406 CE)
nodes.notes: Authored the Muqaddimah & Berber/Arab universal histories; negotiated with Timur at Damascus.

nodes.name: Kaya Maghan Cissé & Tunka Menin of Wagadu / Ghana Empire (8th–11th c. CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Oral Epic of Sundiata, Ibn Khaldun, Al-Umari.

nodes.name: Mansa Sundiata Keita ('Lion King' Founder of Mali Empire; Kouroukan Fouga 1235 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Oral Epic of Sundiata, Ibn Khaldun, Al-Umari.

nodes.name: Mansa Abu Bakr II (Atlantic Navigator Emperor of Mali, c. 1311 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Oral Epic of Sundiata, Ibn Khaldun, Al-Umari.

nodes.name: Mansa Sulayman of Mali (Brother of Mansa Musa; Visited by Ibn Battuta 1352 CE)
nodes.notes: Presided over prosperous Mali; hosted Ibn Battuta.

nodes.name: Emperor Sonni Ali Ber (Conquered Timbuktu & Djenné, 1464–1492 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Tarikh es-Soudan, Modern Universal History Vol. 7.

nodes.name: Emperor Askia Dawud (Songhai Golden Age Scholar-Patron, 1549–1582 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Tarikh es-Soudan, Modern Universal History Vol. 7.

nodes.name: Ahmad Baba al-Timbukti (Chancellor of Sankore University, Timbuktu, 1556–1627 CE)
nodes.major: Descendant of Timbuktu's Aqit scholarly lineage; authored over 40 works.

nodes.name: Queen Magajiya Daurama & Bayajidda (Founders of the Seven Hausa Bakwai States)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Kano Chronicle, Sokoto Caliphate Archives.

nodes.name: Queen Amina / Aminatu of Zazzau (16th c. Hausa Warrior Queen, Kano Chronicle)
nodes.notes: Extended Zazzau dominion from Nupe to Kwararafa and built the legendary Ganuwar Amina walls.

nodes.name: Shehu Usman dan Fodio (Founder of Sokoto Caliphate, 1754–1817 CE)
nodes.notes: Fulani-Torodbe scholar who founded the Sokoto Caliphate in 1804 CE.

nodes.name: Sultan Muhammad Bello & Poet-Scholar Nana Asma'u of Sokoto (1781–1864 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Kano Chronicle, Sokoto Caliphate Archives.

nodes.name: Empress Eleni of Ethiopia (+ Zara Yaqob; Sent 1509 Portuguese Diplomatic Embassy)
nodes.notes: Consort of Zara Yaqob; initiator of the 1509–1520 Ethiopian–Portuguese alliance.

nodes.name: Emperor Fasilides of Ethiopia (Founded Gondar & Fasil Ghebbi Castles, 1632–1667 CE)
nodes.notes: Built the walled imperial city of Gondar in 1636 CE.

nodes.name: Emperor Tewodros II & Empress Taytu Betul (+ Menelik II, Co-Victor of Adwa 1896)
nodes.notes: Tewodros II initiated modern Ethiopian unification; Empress Taytu co-led the 1896 victory at Adwa.

nodes.name: Sultan Ali ibn al-Hassan Shirazi (Founder of Kilwa Sultanate, Swahili Coast, c. 957 CE)
nodes.notes: Shirazi Persian prince who settled East Africa and founded the trading sultanate of Kilwa.

nodes.name: Sultan Sayyid Said bin Sultan of Oman & Zanzibar (1806–1856 CE)
nodes.notes: Moved the Al Bu Said imperial capital to Stone Town, Zanzibar (1840).

nodes.name: Emir Ismail Samani (Founder of Samanid Renaissance of Bukhara, 892–907 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Al-Tabari, Al-Biruni.

nodes.name: Emir Adud al-Dawla (Buyid King of Kings of Shiraz & Baghdad, 949–983 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Al-Tabari, Al-Biruni.

nodes.name: Sultan Ahmad Sanjar (Final Great Seljuk Sultan of Merv, 1118–1157 CE)
nodes.notes: Son of Malik-Shah I.

nodes.name: Shah Ala ad-Din Muhammad II of Khwarazm (1200–1220 CE)
sources: Juvayni History of the World Conqueror
nodes.notes: Ruled Transoxiana & Persia prior to Genghis Khan's 1219 campaign.

nodes.name: Sultan Jalal ad-Din Mangburni (Last Khwarazmshah, Battle of the Indus 1221 CE)
nodes.notes: Fought Genghis Khan at the Indus River (1221 CE).

nodes.name: Ilkhan Hulagu Khan (Grandson of Genghis; Founded Ilkhanate of Persia 1256 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Rashid al-Din Jami' al-Tawarikh, Modern Universal History Vol. 4.

nodes.name: Ilkhans Abaqa Khan & Arghun Khan (Envoys Rabban Bar Sauma & Edward I, 1265–1291)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Rashid al-Din Jami' al-Tawarikh, Modern Universal History Vol. 4.

nodes.name: Ilkhans Ghazan & Öljaitü (+ Vizier Rashid al-Din Jami' al-Tawarikh, 1295–1316 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Rashid al-Din Jami' al-Tawarikh, Modern Universal History Vol. 4.

nodes.name: Shah Rukh & Queen Gawhar Shad (Timurid Herat Renaissance, 1405–1447 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Baburnama, Tarikh-i-Rashidi.

nodes.name: Sultan Ulugh Beg (Samarkand Observatory & Zij-i-Sultani, 1394–1449 CE)
nodes.notes: Computed the length of the sidereal year within 58 seconds at his Samarkand observatory.

nodes.name: Sultan Husayn Bayqara & Poet Ali-Shir Nava'i (1469–1506 CE Herat Court)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Baburnama, Tarikh-i-Rashidi.

nodes.name: Reza Shah Pahlavi → Mohammad Reza Shah Pahlavi of Iran (1925–1979 CE)
nodes.notes: 20th-century imperial dynasty succeeding Qajar Iran.

nodes.name: Khan Berke of the Golden Horde (Allied with Mamluk Baybars, 1257–1266 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Abulghazi, Modern Universal History Vol. 4.

nodes.name: Khan Öz Beg of the Golden Horde (Longest Reign; Golden Age of Sarai, 1313–1341 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Abulghazi, Modern Universal History Vol. 4.

nodes.name: Khan Tokhtamysh (Rival of Timur; Restorer of Golden Horde, 1380–1395 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Abulghazi, Modern Universal History Vol. 4.

nodes.name: Khans Hacı I & Meñli I Giray of Crimea (+ Ayşe Hafsa Sultan, Mother of Suleiman I)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Abulghazi, Modern Universal History Vol. 4.

nodes.name: Muhammad Shaybani Khan (Founder of Uzbek Shaybanid Dynasty of Bukhara, 1451–1510)
nodes.notes: Jochid descendant of Batu/Shiban; rival of Babur.

nodes.name: Khans Kerey & Janibek (Founders of the Kazakh Khanate, 1465 CE)
nodes.notes: Jochid/Orda-Iden princes who established the Kazakh Khanate.

nodes.name: Khan Ablai of the Kazakhs (1711–1781 CE)
nodes.role: Great Khan of all Three Kazakh Jüz
nodes.notes: United the Senior, Middle & Junior Kazakh Jüz.

nodes.name: Khan Kuchum of Siberia (Final Chinggisid Khan of the Khanate of Sibir, d. c. 1601 CE)
nodes.notes: Last Shaybanid-Chinggisid sovereign of Western Siberia.

nodes.name: King Rezon of Damascus (1 Kings 11:23–25; Solomon's Adversary)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in 1–2 Kings, Tel Dan Stele, Assyrian Royal Inscriptions.

nodes.name: King Ben-Hadad I of Aram-Damascus (1 Kings 15:18)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in 1–2 Kings, Tel Dan Stele, Assyrian Royal Inscriptions.

nodes.name: King Ben-Hadad II / Hadadezer (Battle of Qarqar 853 BCE vs Shalmaneser III; 1 Kgs 20)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in 1–2 Kings, Tel Dan Stele, Assyrian Royal Inscriptions.

nodes.name: King Hazael of Aram-Damascus (Tel Dan Stele 'House of David', 2 Kgs 8:15, c. 842–796 BCE)
nodes.notes: Erected the Tel Dan Stele bearing the oldest extra-biblical reference to 'BYTDWD' (House of David).

nodes.name: King Ben-Hadad III (Son of Hazael, 2 Kgs 13:3)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in 1–2 Kings, Tel Dan Stele, Assyrian Royal Inscriptions.

nodes.name: King Rezin of Damascus (Syro-Ephraimite War, Isa 7:1, 2 Kgs 16:9)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in 1–2 Kings, Tel Dan Stele, Assyrian Royal Inscriptions.

nodes.name: King Mesha of Moab (Mesha Stele / Moabite Stone, 2 Kgs 3:4, c. 840 BCE)
nodes.notes: Carved the Moabite Stone recording Omri, Chemosh & House of David.

nodes.name: Kings Nahash & Hanun of Ammon (1 Sam 11, 2 Sam 10)
nodes.notes: Ammonite kings descended from Ben-Ammi son of Lot.

nodes.name: King Baalis of Ammon (Jeremiah 40:14, 6th c. BCE Seal Verified)
nodes.notes: Attested archaeologically on Ammonite royal official Milkom'ur seal.

nodes.name: King Achish of Gath & Kings of Ashdod/Gaza (1 Sam 21, 27, 29)
nodes.notes: Sheltered young David at Ziklag.

nodes.name: King Ikausu / Achish of Ekron (Ekron Royal Dedicatory Inscription, 7th c. BCE)
nodes.notes: Named in Esarhaddon/Ashurbanipal prism & Ekron foundation inscription.

nodes.name: Kings Aramu & Sarduri I of Urartu (Founders of Tushpa / Lake Van, c. 858–824 BCE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Urartian Cuneiform Inscriptions, Khorenatsi.

nodes.name: King Menua of Urartu (Shamiram Canal & Cuneiform Inscriptions, 810–786 BCE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Urartian Cuneiform Inscriptions, Khorenatsi.

nodes.name: King Argishti I of Urartu (Founded Erebuni / Yerevan 782 BCE)
nodes.notes: Built the fortress of Erebuni in 782 BCE, direct origin of Armenia's capital Yerevan.

nodes.name: King Sarduri II of Urartu (Peak Extent vs Tiglath-Pileser III, 764–735 BCE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Urartian Cuneiform Inscriptions, Khorenatsi.

nodes.name: Kings Rusa I & Rusa II (Musasir & Teishebaini vs Sargon II, 735–645 BCE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Urartian Cuneiform Inscriptions, Khorenatsi.

nodes.name: Kings Gordias & Midas of Phrygia ('Mita of Mushki', d. c. 696 BCE)
nodes.notes: Historical King Midas wed a Greek princess of Cyme and corresponded with Sargon II of Assyria.

nodes.name: King Gyges of Lydia ('Gugu' in Ashurbanipal Annals, 680–644 BCE)
nodes.notes: Sent mercenaries to Egypt's Psamtik I and envoys to Nineveh.

nodes.name: King Alyattes of Lydia (Eclipse of Thales Battle 585 BCE; Father of Croesus)
nodes.notes: Coined earliest electrum money; father of Croesus.

nodes.name: Queen Artemisia I of Halicarnassus & Satrap Mausolus of Caria (Mausoleum)
nodes.notes: Naval commander at Salamis (480 BCE) and builder of the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus.

nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Almanach de Gotha, Koninklijk Huis.

nodes.notes: Direct imperial princes elevated under Habsburg Holy Roman Emperors continuing in 2026.

nodes.notes: U.S. Presidential father-and-son dynasty.

nodes.notes: Preserved the Union and issued the Emancipation Proclamation (1863).

nodes.name: Presidents Theodore Roosevelt & Franklin D. Roosevelt (Delano / House of Lannoy → Charlemagne)
nodes.notes: Connected via Philippe de Lannoy (Delano) into European nobility & Charlemagne.

nodes.role: Liberator of Gran Colombia, Peru & Bolivia

nodes.notes: Direct Portuguese Braganza & Austrian Habsburg line (Dom Pedro I wed Archduchess Leopoldina, sister of Marie Louise).
